trends.trend: Federal debt-service squeeze: ~6%-of-GDP deficits, interest above defense, higher long rates
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Interest on the debt already exceeds defence and is the fastest-growing federal outlay; 10-year Treasuries above 5% (Nov 2026) feed straight into mortgage, car-loan and business rates and leave less room for everything else government does.

trends.trend: Entitlement cliffs and benefit retrenchment (Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, SNAP, ACA)
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Dated cliffs and rule changes hit households directly: Medicaid work rules from 1 Jan 2027, SNAP costs shifted to states from FY2028, lapsed ACA subsidies, Highway Trust Fund exhaustion in 2028, and the 2032-33 Social Security and Medicare hospital-fund depletion dates that dominate late-decade politics.

trends.trend: Tax and tariff regime churn: OBBBA sunsets, court-voided tariffs, refunds, yearly IRS resets
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Take-home pay and prices move with law: tip, overtime and senior deductions expire after 2028, tariffs were voided by the Supreme Court and re-imposed under other statutes, importers chase refunds, and brackets reset each November.

trends.trend: State and local budget stress and federal cost-shifting (deficits, pensions, service cuts)
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: States must balance budgets while absorbing federal cost-shifts: California's structural gap (about $35bn a year from 2027-28 on the LAO's November 2025 numbers), New York out-year gaps and pension contributions translate into tuition, transit, school and clinic decisions people see locally.

trends.trend: Government adoption and regulation of AI on binding timetables
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Whether a benefit claim, job application or loan is decided by software, and what notice and appeal a person gets, is being fixed by statutes with start dates (Colorado 1 Jan 2027; EU 2 Dec 2027 and 2 Aug 2028) while Washington buys AI tools government-wide and sues to pre-empt state rules.

latest_edition.title: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036

sources.update_cadence: Annual (Jan/Feb), usually with a mid-year update; reposted with corrections March 2026 (the govinfo copy saved here was created 2026-03-20). Secondary sources report a CBO trade-policy update (policy through 31 July 2026) adding $0.9tn to 2027-36 deficits; could not be downloaded.

accuracy.why: Passes T3 (CBO scores itself: regular forecast-accuracy and 'evaluation of past deficit and debt projections' reports) and T4 (the baseline is a statutory 10-year projection under section 202(e) of the Budget Act). No money or licence at stake (T1 fails), nobody is paid to attack it (T2 fails), and the outcome is not in the pipeline because Congress legislates against the baseline. Known directional issue: the current-law convention (e.g. it must assume benefits are paid in full after trust-fund exhaustion and treats tariffs set by executive action as permanent); nine days after publication the Supreme Court voided the IEEPA tariffs it had booked as $3.0tn of deficit reduction, and it assumed a 4.1% 10-year Treasury rate for 2026 against 5.10% on 2026-11-17 in the Treasury CSV saved under treasury-market-pricing.

richness.why: 172 pages: every major programme by fiscal year, named laws (2025 reconciliation act, tariffs, immigration actions), trust-fund exhaustion dates, enrolment trends, economic assumptions and uncertainty analysis, changes since last baseline.

ai.why: Feb 2026 edition. Generative AI is a named, quantified driver of the economic forecast (+0.1 pp TFP growth a year, +1% nonfarm business output by 2036; AI capex lifts 2026 investment) but nothing on the budget side (no AI effect on outlays, revenues by source or the federal workforce), so material driver with partial quantification rather than a full line item.

ai_passage.text: In CBO’s projections, annual TFP growth from 2026 to 2036 is 0.1 percentage point higher than it would have been without the additional contribution from generative AI diffusion; that faster growth increases the level of output in the nonfarm business sector by 1 percent in 2036.

ai_evidence.search_note: Searched full report for 'artificial intelligence', 'generative AI', 'AI': 25 matching lines, all in the economic chapter (productivity, business investment, interest rates, uncertainty).

sources.why_top_or_not: The reference baseline every other US fiscal forecast is measured against; richest year-by-year detail and the only official US fiscal projection that quantifies an AI productivity effect.
